hints: Look closely at which strand contains U and which strands contain only T, and notice where the strands are paired and where they are separated in the bubble.
Remember that mRNA is complementary to the transcribed (template) strand and almost identical to the non-transcribed (coding) strand, with U in RNA replacing T in DNA.
walkthrough:
**Spot the three strands in the bubble**

Look at the bottom circle C first. There you see normal DNA base pairs like T-A and C-G. That is DNA still wound up ahead of transcription, since the direction arrow points upwards.

In the middle the DNA is unwound. You can see a short strand with U bases. Any strand with U must be RNA.

**Identify mRNA and the template strand**

The middle strand D contains U and in its lower part is paired to the right-hand strand B. Check the pairing:
$$C-G, A-T, C-G, G-C, G-C$$
That is perfect complementary pairing between RNA and DNA. So D is the new mRNA and B is the DNA strand it is using as a template. B is therefore the transcribed strand.

**Find the strand that matches mRNA**

The left-hand strand A is displaced and not paired in the bubble. It contains only DNA bases, T, A, C, G, with no U. Its sequence C-A-C-G-G matches the mRNA sequence C-A-C-G-G.

A strand that is the same as mRNA, except T instead of U, and is not used as a template is the coding strand. That is the non-transcribed strand, so the answer is A.

options.A: Correct. This left DNA strand has only T, not U, is not paired to mRNA, and its base sequence matches the mRNA, which is exactly what the non-transcribed coding strand does.
options.B: This is the transcribed template strand on the right. It pairs directly with the growing mRNA in the bubble, so it is used for transcription.
options.C: This is intact double-stranded DNA ahead of the polymerase, with normal T-A and C-G pairs, not a single separated strand.
options.D: This middle strand contains U bases, so it is the new mRNA molecule being made, not a DNA strand.
